plain_description.what: On 242 questions where models disagree, the judge was allowed to abstain (score as a coin flip) whenever the reference answer's own confidence fell below a threshold. Several thresholds were compared with always answering.
plain_description.why: The judge goes badly wrong when the reference answer misleads it. The test asks whether the reference's own confidence can flag those cases in advance.
plain_description.information: A win would give a cheap safety valve for the judge. A loss would close another confidence-based fix. Result: negative (no new calls). Confidence does carry signal: the reference is right 48% of the time below 90 and 90% at 100. But every abstention threshold scores lower than always answering, because abstaining throws away more wins than losses. This is the third confidence-based fix to fail. It is on the older judged data, which the author has since ruled history rather than evidence.
